meta.title: As Much World As Fits
meta.subtitle: A snapshot is not the world — it is a prioritised prefix of the world, cut off wherever the packet ends

views.label: Order first, then encode
views.note: The chunk list is sorted before a single bit is written, so the packet fills in priority order.

views.label: The delta is per connection
views.note: Every client has acknowledged a different tick, so the server keeps a different baseline set for each one.

views.label: Where the world gets cut
views.note: Writing stops when the bits run out. Everything below the line simply waits, with its priority rising.

views.label: Landing on the client
views.note: Bytes go into a per-ghost ring. A separate system decides which tick to read them at.

nodes.label: Below the cut
nodes.sublabel: not lost, just not this tick

nodes.label: Ghost update
nodes.sublabel: read the ring at this ghost's tick

cards.title: The five steps, in the order they run
items: Sort the ghost chunks for this one connection by priority
For each entity pick up to three acknowledged baselines and delta against them
Write entropy coded bits into the packet until the budget is gone
The client decodes against the same baselines and writes into a per-ghost ring
A separate system reads that ring at whichever tick the ghost's timeline names

cards.title: Why the cut is a feature
items: There is one packet per connection per network tick and it has a hard ceiling
Whatever did not fit keeps ageing, so its priority climbs and it goes next time
Starvation is prevented by the age term, not by a queue
This is bus arbitration: everyone wants the bus, priority and age decide who gets it

cards.title: The baseline is what makes it small
items: The server remembers what each connection last acknowledged, separately
Three baselines let it extrapolate a prediction and send only the residual
A near-zero residual costs a handful of bits, so constant velocity is almost free
The history is thirty two slots, sized for about half a second of round trip

cards.title: What it looks like when it goes wrong
items: Cannot fit even one ghost: the packet size doubles and the whole thing is re-serialised
Acks stop arriving: baselines age out, deltas get large, bandwidth climbs
Too few chunks examined per tick: the packet goes out half empty
A ghost that vanishes and reappears usually left the relevant set, it did not despawn
